chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Maymun al-Qaddah, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no act of worship superior to restraining the belly and the private parts.'
ai.seo_question: What is considered the most superior act of worship in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies 'iffah' (chastity/restraint) of the belly and private parts as the pinnacle of worship, shifting the focus from ritualistic acts to the foundational discipline of the self. This concept underscores the Shia understanding that moral purity is the prerequisite for all other acts of devotion, reflecting the principle that guarding one's sanctity invites divine protection. The narration highlights the interplay between human effort in self-restraint and God's reciprocal guarding of the believer's honor.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, form Maymoun Al Qaddah who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is none from the (acts of) worship superior than restraint of the belly and the private parts’.
en.sarwar: 7. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab from Maymun al-Qaddah who has said the following: “I once heard abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
No worship is better than maintaining chastity in matters of one’s stomach and genitals organs.’”
